about:
DTIS Techs Diesel Parts operates from Salt Lake City, Utah. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company remanufactures a full line of diesel components, including injectors, turbochargers, fuel pumps, oil pumps, EGR coolers, electronic actuators, and accessory and contamination kits. Technicians are trained on specific injector lines and turbos, and most remanufactured injectors receive new trim code programming. No facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures are published.

While the company does not list specific industry verticals, its product range serves the diesel repair and maintenance market, including heavy-duty trucking, construction equipment, agricultural machinery, and fleet maintenance operations.

DTIS Techs emphasizes quality through specialized technician training and trim code programming on injectors. It backs products with a standard 12-month, unlimited-mileage warranty, an optional 18-month extended warranty, free ground shipping, and a 45-day core return policy for core charge refunds.

name: DZEE Textiles | Hotel Supplies & Hospitality Products Wholesale
old_description: For the best experience on our site, be sure to turn on Javascript in your browser.
about:
DZEE Textiles LLC operates from Orlando, Florida, where it was established more than 25 years ago as a wholesale distributor of hotel supplies. The company began with a vision to provide high-quality, affordable hospitality products directly to the industry, bypassing intermediaries.

The company distributes a broad range of hospitality goods — bath linens, pool and gym towels, bed sheets, pillow cases, duvets, blankets, decorative bedding, bath amenities, guest-room appliances, and janitorial supplies. It sources products using what it describes as state-of-the-art technology and applies rigorous quality-control measures. DZEE Textiles reports serving more than 10,000 customers, including hotels, motels, resorts, vacation rentals, salons, and casinos, and emphasizes direct factory pricing with free delivery on orders over $999 in most areas.

Its customer base spans the hospitality sector, specifically hotels, motels, resorts, vacation rentals, salons, and casinos. The company highlights long-standing relationships with hospitality buyers and hotel managers built on trust and mutual respect.

DZEE Textiles says it differentiates itself through unbeatable prices, high durability, and fast, free delivery. It also points to eco-friendly manufacturing processes and sustainable material sourcing as part of its commitment to responsible business practices.

about:
Daedalus Industrial is based in Easley, South Carolina. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year, ownership structure, or founders.

The company manufactures custom control panels through build-to-print and custom design services, with in-house fabrication optimized for rapid deployment. It delivers automation solutions including SCADA and IoT system development, robotic integration with collaborative robotics and vision systems, modular motion and process control, and advanced analytics with AI-driven predictive maintenance and adaptive machine vision. Daedalus also operates as a licensed electrical contractor specializing in low- and ultra-low-voltage systems, building management systems, power management, structured cabling, and industrial networking. Additional capabilities encompass OT cybersecurity risk assessments, secure architecture design, network segmentation, compliance audits aligned with NIST and IEC 62443, and controls-centric installation services for third-party OEM equipment.

Daedalus serves data centers, utilities, industrial infrastructure, and manufacturing sectors, providing mission-critical solutions for high-availability environments. Its customer base includes original equipment manufacturers and capital project teams seeking turnkey automation, from prototype through production.

The company emphasizes right-sized, future-proof engineering that balances efficiency with efficacy, avoiding unnecessary complexity. Its differentiators include modular, scalable designs, in-house data science expertise for lean AI integration, and a responsive, agile approach to custom fabrication and controls engineering.

name: Dakota Carding
old_description: offers you custom fiber processing of your wool, animal fibers, exotics and misc. fibers. This is a cottage industry carding mill providing you with affordable custom washing and carding of your animal/plant/pet fibers.
about:
Dakota Carding operates as a cottage industry carding mill in Groton, South Dakota, specializing in custom fiber processing for individual producers and fiber artists. The company, also known as Dakota Carding & Wool Co., processes wool, animal fibers, exotic fibers, and plant-based materials through washing and carding services.

Its core operations center on a Dyna Card Mill that provides custom washing and carding of customer-supplied fibers. In addition to contract processing, the mill produces its own carded wool blends, handspun and millspun yarns, and sheepskins. The facility also retails spinning wheels, looms, knitting needles, and finished wearable art under the Biotayarns label. All fibers are sourced domestically, with an emphasis on local prairie-inspired color blends.

The customer base includes hand spinners, felters, and small-scale fiber producers seeking affordable custom carding for their own clips, as well as hobbyists purchasing ready-to-spin blends and equipment. The mill serves both individual fiber growers who send in raw fleece and retail customers looking for unique yarns and spinning supplies.

The business highlights its affordable, small-batch processing and domestic sourcing as key differentiators. The current owners have listed the carding mill for sale, indicating a transition opportunity for the operation.

name: Dakota Timber Company - Sustainable Wood Products & Home Goods - Made In the USA
old_description: Our lumber materials are sourced primarily from agricultural buildings in the upper Midwest or from urban tree removals.
about:
Dakota Timber Company operates from Horace, North Dakota, where it produces a line of reclaimed wood products for residential and commercial projects. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, but its roots are tied to the upper Midwest's agricultural heritage.

The shop manufactures fireplace mantels, floating shelf kits, structural beams, shiplap paneling, stair treads, brackets, and custom tops. Lumber is sourced primarily from decommissioned agricultural buildings across the upper Midwest and from urban tree removals, then milled and finished in-house. Production is made-to-order with a typical lead time of four to six weeks, and finished goods ship via LTL freight.

Customers include homeowners, builders, and interior designers across the region. Recent project work includes floating shelf installations for Rachel Platt of RP at Home, a fireplace mantel for D Gilpin Properties, white oak shiplap for Klein Custom Homes, and a whole-home package for Studio West's Rose Creek residence in Fargo, North Dakota.

The company positions its output as 100 percent American-made, emphasizing low-impact production and the reuse of materials that would otherwise enter the waste stream. Its floating shelf kits feature a proprietary mounting bracket designed for straightforward installation.

name: Danfoss Power Solutions
old_description: We engineer solutions that increase machine productivity, reduce emissions, lower energy consumption, and enable electrification.
about:
Danfoss Power Solutions operates from Searcy, Arkansas, as part of a global enterprise founded in 1933 by Mads Clausen in Denmark. The company remains family-owned, a structure it says underpins long-term value creation for stakeholders.

The business runs three core segments. Danfoss Power Solutions delivers mobile and industrial hydraulics, fluid conveyance, data-center thermal management, electrification systems, and software. Danfoss Climate Solutions provides energy-efficient heating and cooling for industrial plants, buildings, infrastructure, data centers, and the cold chain. Danfoss Power Electronics and Drives produces power semiconductor modules, variable-speed drives, and power-conversion equipment. Innovation is vetted through 13 Application Development Centers worldwide where customers test solutions in live environments.

Customers span mobile machinery, industrial automation, data-center operators, construction, commercial refrigeration, and general industrial markets. Publicly cited collaborations include an energy-efficient AI supercomputer with HPE and a 30 percent energy-saving project with Smardt for chiller systems.

Danfoss states its engineering focus is on increasing machine productivity, cutting emissions, lowering energy consumption, and enabling electrification. The family ownership model, it says, allows massive reinvestment in innovation and digitalization while maintaining a philanthropic commitment through its foundations.

name: Dangar Engineering & Mfg.
old_description: Dangar Engineering specializes in large precision CNC machining, including 5-axis milling of complex parts and tooling. Products serve aerospace, automotive, medical and commercial industries.
about:
Dangar Engineering & Mfg. has operated from Ventura, California since its founding in 1954. The company was established with a focus on mastering the edge of machining technology, choosing to specialize in the difficult and unusual parts that other shops could not produce.

The shop provides large precision CNC machining, including 5-axis milling of complex parts, tooling, prototypes, and production runs. Its equipment includes 5-axis machines with a 242-inch by 115-inch by 25-inch machining envelope (part envelope up to 242 by 115 by 72 inches) and a coordinate measuring machine with a 161.75 by 54 by 53.375-inch inspection envelope, all housed in a 24-hour temperature-controlled facility. Design and NC programming are performed using CATIA CAD/CAM. The company employs 50 to 99 people and also offers inspection, reverse engineering, complex assemblies, welding, and fabrication.

Dangar serves aerospace, architectural, automotive, commercial, medical, and marine industries. Its customer approvals include Northrop Grumman, Lockheed Martin, Litton, Volvo, BMW, Volkswagen, and Pilkington Aerospace. Machined parts are used in commercial and military aerospace applications as well as titanium components implanted in the human body.

The company's stated philosophy is to be a reliable source of high-precision, close-tolerance products with exceptional quality, positioning itself as a one-stop shop for any-angle 5-axis holes and very complex geometry.

about:
Dar Collision Parts is a family-owned-and-operated distributor of automotive collision parts based in St. Albans, West Virginia. Founded in 1991, the company has over three decades of experience in the auto body parts service industry.

The company operates as a distributor of replacement collision parts, including rust repair panels, grilles, bumpers, fenders, header panels, bedsides, doors, and headlight bezels. It also supplies a comprehensive line of automotive exterior lighting as a distributor of TYC and Globe Lighting products, stocking headlights, sidemarkers, park lamps, and taillights for many cars and trucks. In addition, Dar Collision Parts carries a range of truck and SUV accessories such as nerf bars, bedliners, tonneau covers, custom cowl hoods, bug shields, headlight and taillight covers, stepmates, aluminum bed protection, and tool boxes. The firm purchases directly from numerous manufacturers and maintains a large in-stock inventory.

Dar Collision Parts serves the automotive aftermarket, primarily collision repair shops, auto body shops, and truck and SUV owners seeking replacement parts and accessories. Its product range addresses needs from accident-related body panel replacement to lighting upgrades and accessory installation.

The company emphasizes providing superior quality at a lower cost to the automotive aftermarket, leveraging direct manufacturer relationships and a large in-stock inventory to meet customer needs promptly.

name: Darn It Inc
old_description: offered by Darn It! From Storage to Inventory Management and Logistics, We do it all!
about:
Darn It! Inc. operates from New Bedford, Massachusetts, where it was established in 1996 by Jeff Glassman. Glassman launched the business after his family’s apparel factory lost the majority of its workforce to lower-cost competitors in Mexico; a former customer asked him to repair 30,000 damaged trousers, prompting the creation of a company focused on refurbishing clothing. The firm remains family-run.

The company provides warehousing, distribution, and refurbishment services. Its quality-control offerings include 100% inspection of soft lines and hard goods, labeling, sewing repairs, button and snap replacement, cleaning (with an ozone room for odor removal), laundering, mold remediation, pressing, packaging, kitting, and reverse logistics such as returns processing and restocking. The warehouse and distribution arm accounts for roughly 40 percent of revenue and serves more than 20 clients, handling merchandise that ranges from apparel to books and watches.

Customers include retailers, manufacturers, wholesalers, and web-based businesses worldwide. In one case, Darn It! corrected 1,200 mislabeled shirts for a retailer; in another, it inspected 8,000 sets of blackout curtains, recovering 91 percent as sellable inventory through inspection, sewing repairs, and spot cleaning.

Glassman started the business to fill a gap in repairing damaged goods from overseas production, and the company emphasizes quick turnaround to support lean inventory programs for its clients.
